CNC Machining Twin: replay & monitoring

Drill-tap center · outer-contour finishing (rectangle + 4 chamfers) · vibration, load current, actual position
Visualization-level twin. Everything here is replayed from recorded sensor data; it is not a physics-based simulation and does not predict tool or part behaviour. Anomaly, not defect, detection: with only 2 labelled defect runs, the Isolation Forest / One-Class SVM scores identify behaviour that is unusual relative to the training runs. They cannot be claimed to predict defects. Data issues & method →

Runs, ranked by anomaly risk

Risk = share of cutting-phase windows above the amber threshold (mean of both models). ≈5% is typical for a normal run.

Machine view

Top view from actual X/Y position (mm); side view shows actual Z. Rail glow = vibration RMS relative to the normal-run 99th percentile. Markers = cutting windows above threshold.

Health indicator

Latest completed 1 s window. Thresholds: amber = 95th, red = 99th percentile of training-run cutting windows (scored out-of-run).

Anomaly score over the run

Higher = more unusual. Grey spans are outside model scope (not cutting). Click to seek.

Signals

Vibration RMS per 100 ms (DC removed, mg) and axis load current (controller units). Cursor = replay time.

Run summary

Statistics over the two contour passes only (same scope as the models; rapid moves and tool approach excluded). Vibration has the per-run DC offset removed. Range = 10th–90th percentile of training runs.

Comparison

X-axis = aligned process time: each run is time-warped onto the median normal run using G-code line anchors, so the same contour segment lines up even when feeds differ.

Fleet: anomaly risk by run

Each mark is a run. Click a mark or a table row to open its replay. Dashed line = 5%, the rate expected for a typical training run by construction.
